posts.topic: Seven CTAs in forty words
posts.why: Everyone has written this caption, so the shame lands as recognition.

tiktok.hook: This post has seven calls to action in forty words. That means it has none.
tiktok.vo: This post has seven calls to action in forty words. Link in bio, DM me, comment below, call this number, book a slot, save it, share it. When you ask for seven things, the reader does nothing, because choosing is work. One post, one ask. Everything else is noise you paid attention to write.
tiktok.cap: Seven asks is not ambition. It is indecision, published.

instagram.cap: Ask for one thing. The other six are why nobody did anything.

facebook.body:
A caption I saw this week had seven calls to action in forty words: link in bio, DM me, comment below, call, book, save, share.

Seven asks is not ambition. It is indecision, published.

When you ask for seven things, the reader does nothing, because choosing is work.

One post, one ask. Write the other six down for another day.

What is the one thing you want people to do?

posts.topic: One post, one job
posts.why: The simplest rule in the whole month, stated flatly.

tiktok.hook: One post, one job: entertain, teach, or sell. Pick one.
tiktok.vo: One post, one job. Entertain, teach, or sell. Pick one and commit to it, because the post that tries to do two does neither well. The one that entertains and then asks for money loses the entertainment. The one that teaches and then sells loses the teaching. Pick one job and let the next post do the other.
tiktok.cap: A post that does two jobs does neither.

instagram.cap: Three jobs, eleven posts a day, one job each.

facebook.body:
One post, one job.

Entertain. Teach. Or sell.

Pick one and commit, because a post that tries to do two does neither well. The one that entertains and then asks for money loses the entertainment. The one that teaches and then sells loses the teaching.

Your next post can do the other job.

Which of the three do you default to?

posts.topic: The one-word CTA
posts.why: A copyable mechanic, not advice.

tiktok.hook: Use one word as your call to action. Not four sentences of them.
beats: They type it, then everything else happens
tiktok.vo: Use one word as your call to action. Not link in bio, DM me, call, comment. One word in capitals: BUNDLE. They type it in the chat and a person replies. That word is a key, and a key is easier to turn than a paragraph of instructions. Test it for a week and count the messages.
tiktok.cap: One word in capitals. They type it. A human replies. That is the whole funnel.

slides: Not: link in bio · DM · call
instagram.cap: A key is easier to turn than a paragraph.

facebook.body:
Use one word as your call to action.

Not 'link in bio, DM me, call, comment'. One word, in capitals: BUNDLE.

They type it in the chat, a person replies, and the conversation starts properly. That word is a key, and a key is far easier to turn than a paragraph of instructions.

Try it for a week and count the messages.

What would your one word be?

posts.topic: "Only 2 left" with 40 left
posts.why: Names a practice the audience has caught others doing.

tiktok.hook: "Only two left" when there are forty left is the end of your credibility.
beats: Now nothing you say is true
tiktok.vo: Only two left, when there are forty left, is the end of your credibility. People check. They always check, because they have been lied to before. And once one number on your page is invented, every other number becomes a guess, including the price, which was true. Fake scarcity does not create urgency, it creates suspicion.
tiktok.cap: One invented number makes every true number look invented.

instagram.cap: Fake scarcity does not create urgency. It creates suspicion.

facebook.body:
'Only two left', when there are forty left, is the end of your credibility.

People check. They always check, because they have been lied to before.

And once one number on your page is invented, every other number becomes a guess — including the price, which was true.

Fake scarcity does not create urgency. It creates suspicion.

Have you ever caught a shop doing this?

posts.topic: Six packs, no price in the caption
posts.why: A mechanic with a real result attached, and no overclaiming.

tiktok.hook: A post sold six packs with no price in the caption at all.
beats: Because the caption is for everyone
The comment is for the ready
tiktok.vo: A post sold six packs with no price in the caption. The price was in the pinned comment. That was the whole trick. The caption stayed useful to the people who were never going to buy, and the people who were ready found the number one tap away. Same post, two audiences, nobody annoyed.
tiktok.cap: Price in the pinned comment. Six sales. The caption stayed readable.

instagram.cap: Serve the ready without lecturing everyone else.

facebook.body:
A post sold six packs with no price in the caption. The price was in the pinned comment.

That was the entire trick.

The caption stayed useful to the people who were never going to buy. The people who were ready found the number one tap away.

Same post, two audiences, nobody annoyed.

What is in your first comment usually?

posts.topic: Sell the limit
posts.why: The most transferable idea of the week, usable outside our packs.

tiktok.hook: Sell the limit, not the dream. "It will not get you customers" sells better than a promise.
beats: A limit sounds like a person
tiktok.vo: Sell the limit, not the dream. It will not get you customers, it will stop you losing the ones you have. That sentence sells better than any promise, because every ad promises and almost none admit a boundary. A limit sounds like a person telling the truth, and once they trust the limit, they trust the price.
tiktok.cap: A limit sounds like a person. A promise sounds like an ad.

instagram.cap: Say what it will not do. That is where trust starts.

facebook.body:
Sell the limit, not the dream.

'It will not get you customers — it will stop you losing the ones you already have.'

That sentence outsells any promise, because every ad promises and almost none admit a boundary. A limit sounds like a person telling the truth. Once they trust the limit, they trust the price.

What is the honest limit of what you sell?

posts.topic: The caption for people who already want it
posts.why: Splits the audience in a way people have never considered.

tiktok.hook: Your caption explains the offer to the people who already want it.
beats: They do not need the paragraph
The paragraph is for the others
tiktok.vo: Your caption explains the offer to the people who already want it. They do not need explaining. They need the link, in the first three lines, so they can act before their attention drifts. The explanation is for the ones who are not sure yet, and it can come after. Two groups, one order: price, then paragraph.
tiktok.cap: Price first. Paragraph second. Two groups, one order.

slides: Already want it: need the link
instagram.cap: Stop explaining to people who already decided.

facebook.body:
Your caption usually explains the offer to the people who already want it.

They do not need explaining. They need the link, in the first three lines, before their attention drifts.

The explanation is for the people who are not sure yet, and it can come after.

Two groups, one order: price first, paragraph second.

Which group do you write for?

posts.topic: What made you buy the last thing online?
posts.why: Unprompted witnesses saying the same thing as our teaching.

tiktok.hook: I asked what made people buy the last thing they bought online.
beats: I could see what it was
tiktok.vo: I asked what made people buy the last thing they bought online. Nobody said the copywriting. Nobody said the design. Two things came up again and again: I could see what it was, and I could see what it cost. That is the entire job of a page, and it is smaller than most people's websites.
tiktok.cap: "I could see what it was and what it cost." Nothing else came up.

instagram.cap: Visibility and price. Everything else is decoration you chose.

facebook.body:
I asked people what made them buy the last thing they bought online.

Nobody said the copywriting. Nobody said the design.

Two answers came up again and again: 'I could see what it was' and 'I could see what it cost'.

That is the entire job of a page, and it is far smaller than most people's websites.

Can a stranger do both on yours in five seconds?

posts.topic: The bundle buys nothing new
posts.why: The most counterintuitive honest ad of the month.

tiktok.hook: The bundle is thirty-five thousand naira and it buys you nothing new.
tiktok.vo: The bundle is thirty five thousand naira and it buys you nothing new. Same nine packs, ten thousand naira cheaper than buying them separately, and one decision instead of nine. That is the whole offer. It is not a course, not a community, not a call. If you only need one pack, buy one pack, because the bundle is for people who want all of it.
tiktok.cap: ₦35,000. Same nine packs, one decision. Buy one pack if you need one. BUNDLE on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

instagram.cap: If you need one pack, buy one pack. The bundle is for the undecided.

facebook.body:
The bundle is ₦35,000 and it buys you nothing new.

Same nine packs, ₦10,000 cheaper than buying them separately, and one decision instead of nine.

That is the whole offer. Not a course, not a community, not a call.

If you only need one pack, buy one pack. The bundle is for people who want all of it and would rather decide once.

BUNDLE on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.topic: Promising results in the ad
posts.why: Explains why our copy reads the way it does, which builds trust in all of it.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked us to promise results in the ad. We said no and wrote the limit instead.
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to write a promise into an ad. We said no. Promises convert, then they refund, then they resent you, and in a small market the resentment is more expensive than the sale. So we wrote the limit instead: this will not get you customers, it will stop you losing the ones you have. Fewer clicks. Better customers.
tiktok.cap: Promises convert once and cost you twice.

instagram.cap: A promise sells the first time and ruins the second.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to write a promise into an ad.

We said no. Promises convert, then they refund, then they resent you — and in a small market the resentment is more expensive than the sale ever was.

So we wrote the limit instead: this will not get you customers, it will help you keep the ones you have.

Fewer clicks. Better customers. No refunds.

Would you rather be believed or clicked?

posts.topic: Price in the first three lines
posts.why: Concrete and immediately testable on tonight's post.

tiktok.hook: Put the price in the first three lines of the caption. Always.
beats: They will not find line nine
tiktok.vo: Put the price in the first three lines of the caption. Always. Not because everyone is ready, but because the ones who are ready will not scroll to line nine to find it, and the rest of the caption is for everyone else anyway. Hiding the price does not create curiosity, it creates a search.
tiktok.cap: Three lines. Price in one of them. The rest is for the curious.

instagram.cap: Hiding the price creates a search, not curiosity.

facebook.body:
Put the price in the first three lines of your caption.

Always.

Not because everyone is ready, but because the people who are ready will not scroll to line nine to find it. The rest of the caption is for everyone else anyway.

Hiding the price does not create curiosity. It creates a search.

Look at your last post. Which line was the price on?

posts.topic: The worst follow-up of the fortnight
posts.why: Closes the follow-up week with the image it opened on.

tiktok.hook: The worst follow-up I saw this fortnight: nine messages, all of them hello.
tiktok.vo: The worst follow-up I saw this fortnight was nine messages long and every single one said hello. No price, no date, no photograph, nothing to reply to. Then, on the ninth, a discount, which is the sound of someone giving up. Nine chances to be useful and not one of them carried anything.
tiktok.cap: Nine hellos, then a discount. That is not follow-up, that is fading out loud.

instagram.cap: If none of your messages carry information, none of them are follow-ups.

facebook.body:
The worst follow-up I saw this fortnight was nine messages long and every one said hello.

No price. No date. No photo. Nothing to reply to. Then on the ninth message, a discount — which is the sound of someone giving up.

Nine chances to be useful, and not one of them carried anything.

What does your follow-up usually say?

posts.topic: Two weeks in, the honest number
posts.why: A public ledger is the most defensible content an account can post.

tiktok.hook: Two weeks in. Here is the number, read off the sheet, including the boring parts.
tiktok.vo: Two weeks in, and here is the number read off the sheet. Most posts did very little. A few did most of the work. The conversations that came from it were fewer than the views by a factor of about a thousand, which is normal and is the part nobody posts about. That is the honest state of it, and I would rather show you the flat line than sell you a hockey stick.
tiktok.cap: Two weeks, read off the sheet. Mostly a flat line, a few spikes, and a thousand views per conversation.

instagram.cap: The flat line is the honest part. Most accounts never show it.

facebook.body:
Two weeks in, and here is the honest number, read off the sheet.

Most posts did very little. A few did most of the work. The conversations that came out of it were roughly a thousand views per conversation, which is normal and is the part nobody posts about.

I would rather show you the flat line than sell you a hockey stick.

What does your own sheet say?

posts.topic: The lesson that got the most saves
posts.why: Re-runs the winner with new material instead of repeating it.

tiktok.hook: The most saved lesson of the fortnight, again, with a different story.
tiktok.vo: The most saved thing I posted this fortnight was the five lines every quote needs. So here it is again with a different example. What it is. How much. By when. What is included. What is not. On a catering quote: jollof for forty, this much, Saturday by noon, plates and serving included, drinks not included. Same five lines, different business.
tiktok.cap: What · How much · By when · Included · Not included. Again, because you saved it.

instagram.cap: The same five lines, applied to catering. Use whichever example is yours.

facebook.body:
The most saved lesson of the last fortnight, again, with a different example.

What it is. How much. By when. What is included. What is not included.

On a catering quote: jollof for forty people, this much, Saturday by noon, plates and serving included, drinks not included.

Same five lines. Different business. Works every time.

Which one do you leave out?

posts.topic: Half of content strategy is answering people
posts.why: Cheap to act on, and quietly deflates the mystique of strategy.

tiktok.hook: Half of what people call content strategy is just answering messages.
tiktok.vo: Half of what people call content strategy is just answering messages in public. Someone asks a question in your chat, you answer it in a post, someone else has the same question, and you have just saved a conversation. Do that forty times and you have a content strategy, a website, and an FAQ, and you did not need a framework.
tiktok.cap: Answer the same question in public forty times. That is the strategy.

instagram.cap: Your inbox is a content calendar you keep ignoring.

facebook.body:
Half of what people call content strategy is just answering messages in public.

Someone asks a question in your chat. You answer it in a post. Someone else has the same question and now you have saved a conversation.

Do that forty times and you have a content strategy, a website and an FAQ — and you never needed a framework.

What did someone ask you this week?

posts.topic: The best thing anyone said to us this fortnight
posts.why: Quoting a customer honestly, with no embellishment.

tiktok.hook: The best thing anyone said to us this fortnight, quoted exactly.
beats: You told me the price in the first line
tiktok.vo: The best thing anyone said to us this fortnight was not a compliment. It was this: you told me the price in the first line, and that is why I messaged you. Which is not flattering, it is a mechanic. But it was the first proof that the thing we had been writing about all week was doing what we said it did, and it came from a stranger, which is the only place proof counts.
tiktok.cap: "You told me the price in the first line. That is why I messaged."

instagram.cap: Not a compliment. A mechanic, confirmed by a stranger.

facebook.body:
The best thing anyone said to us this fortnight:

'You told me the price in the first line, and that is why I messaged you.'

Not flattering. Just a mechanic, confirmed by a stranger — which is the only place proof actually counts.

We had been writing about that all week, and there it was in the inbox.

What is the last thing a customer told you that you did not expect?

posts.topic: What I got wrong this week
posts.why: A correction with no lesson attached is rarer and more credible.

tiktok.hook: What I got wrong this week, with no lesson attached.
beats: I said follow up three times
I did not follow up once
tiktok.vo: What I got wrong this week. I told you to follow up within three days, and then I did not follow up with a single person who messaged me, because I was busy, which is exactly what every customer of yours says. No lesson attached. I just got it wrong, and the advice is still right, which is the uncomfortable part.
tiktok.cap: Told you to follow up in three days. Did not follow up once. No lesson attached.

slides: I said: follow up in 3 days
instagram.cap: "Do as I say" is weaker when you admit you did not.

facebook.body:
What I got wrong this week.

I told you to follow up within three days. Then I did not follow up with a single person who messaged me, because I was busy — which is exactly what every customer of yours says.

No lesson attached. I just got it wrong. The advice is still right, which is the uncomfortable part.

Where are you not doing the thing you tell other people to do?

posts.topic: The post I deleted
posts.why: Transparency about editing builds trust in everything published.

tiktok.hook: I wrote a post this week and deleted it before publishing. Here is why.
beats: It was a joke at someone's expense
tiktok.vo: I wrote a post this week and deleted it before publishing. It was a teardown of a real business and the joke was at their expense, and they would have recognised themselves, which makes it bullying with a screenshot attached. It would have done well. It went in the bin.
tiktok.cap: It would have performed. It would have been cruel. It went in the bin.

instagram.cap: If they would recognise themselves, it is not a teardown. It is a joke at their expense.

facebook.body:
I wrote a post this week and deleted it before publishing.

It was a teardown of a real business and the joke was at their expense. They would have recognised themselves. That makes it bullying with a screenshot attached.

It would have done numbers.

It went in the bin.

What have you not posted because it was true but unkind?

posts.topic: Our own bio, round two
posts.why: Pays off the promise made on day 7.

tiktok.hook: We rewrote our own bio after strangers could not tell what we do. Round two.
beats: Round two said: the people who write your homepage
tiktok.vo: We rewrote our bio after strangers could not tell what we do. Round one said helping brands tell their story, which is what everybody says. Round two says we write the words on your homepage, in eight words or fewer. This time six out of ten knew what we did. Not perfect. Better. The lesson is the same one we give everybody: say the thing, not the feeling.
tiktok.cap: 6 out of 10, up from 3. Say the thing, not the feeling.

instagram.cap: Still not perfect. Much better than poetry.

facebook.body:
We rewrote our own bio after strangers could not tell what we do.

Round one: 'helping brands tell their story.' That is what everybody says.
Round two: 'we write the words on your homepage.'

Six out of ten strangers could now tell us what we do, up from three.

Not perfect. Better. The lesson is the same one we give everybody: say the thing, not the feeling.

What does your bio say?

posts.topic: The project we turned down
posts.why: Pays off day 11 with the same real story, not a new invention.

tiktok.hook: The project we turned down this week was five pages for forty thousand naira.
beats: At that price they get templates
tiktok.vo: The project we turned down this week was five pages for forty thousand naira. At that price, five pages means five templates nobody reads, and I would have been selling them a website-shaped object. So I said what forty thousand actually buys: one page, written properly, working on a phone. They took it. It is the first site they have had enquiries from.
tiktok.cap: Refused five pages. Sold one. It was the honest version of the same job.

instagram.cap: A smaller promise you can keep is worth more than a bigger one you cannot.

facebook.body:
The project we turned down this week was five pages for ₦40,000.

At that price, five pages means five templates nobody reads. I would have been selling a website-shaped object.

So I said what ₦40,000 actually buys: one page, written properly, working on a phone. They took it. It is the first site they have had enquiries from.

When did you last talk someone out of the bigger job?
